chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from Jabr ibn Yazeed, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah used to say:

Indeed, the dream of the believer floats between the sky and the earth over the head of its owner until he interprets it for himself or it is interpreted for him by someone like him. So when it is interpreted, it adheres to the earth. So do not narrate your dreams except to one who understands.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of interpreting dreams in Shia tradition and who should one share them with?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual potency of a believer's vision, describing it as suspended between the heavens and earth until its meaning is realized through interpretation by the dreamer or a knowledgeable peer. The instruction to share only with 'those who understand' (man ya'qil) reflects the Shia emphasis on discernment and the potential for dreams to influence one's spiritual state, necessitating an audience capable of providing accurate, context-aware exegesis.

en.hubeali: H 14976 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Ghalib, from Jabir Bin Yazeed, who has narrated the following: Abu Ja’farasws said that the Rasool Allahsaww had said: ‘

The dream of the Believer floats in between the sky and the earth over the head of its dreamer until he interprets it for himself, or it is interpreted for him by someone like him. So when it gets interpreted, it comes to the ground. So do not narrate your dreams except to the one who understand’.
en.sarwar: 530. Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al-Qasim bin Urwat, from Abu Baseer, who has reported the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said that the Rasool Allah (saww) said: ‘
Do not tell your dream except to a Believer who is free from the envy and the rebellion’.
